headline:
Every bone.
A closer connection.
intro: A three-dimensional atlas of the adult human skeleton. Rotate, discover, and explore the anatomy beneath the surface.
circulationIntro: An interactive model with 676 separate cardiovascular structures. Choose a circuit, select a part, and open its anatomy details.
respiratoryIntro: Explore the lungs, airways, and pharynx in an interactive model. Filter airways or lungs, then select any structure to review its position, function, and airflow route.
digestiveIntro: Explore the digestive tract and accessory organs, from the mouth and esophagus to the intestines, liver, and pancreas. Select a structure for its anatomy details.
combinedHeadline:
The human systems
in one anatomy model
combinedIntro: Explore 206 bones, 676 cardiovascular structures, and 220 respiratory and digestive structures aligned in one anatomical view.
selectVisceralPart: Select a structure on the model to view its details
visceralDetailsOverview: This mesh corresponds to “{{name}}” in the Z-Anatomy atlas and is classified as {{system}}.
visceralDetailsLocation: The 3D model shows the structure's anatomical position and its source category ({{category}}).
visceralDetailsCaveat: This is an educational model, not a clinical reference. Microscopic structures such as alveoli and intestinal villi are not separately modeled, and geometry alone does not show complete physiological function.
visceralDetailsReference: Names and geometry come from the credited Z-Anatomy / BodyParts3D model. These concise educational descriptions do not replace medical references.
visceralDisclaimer: 220 selectable respiratory and digestive structures, including shared pharyngeal parts. For anatomy education, not diagnosis or treatment.
combinedDisclaimer: 4 anatomically aligned systems: 206 bones, 676 cardiovascular structures, and 220 respiratory and digestive structures. Educational use only.

visceralFunction.respiratoryAirway: Part of the passages that conduct air between the nose or mouth and the lungs. Conducting, warming, and humidifying roles vary with the structure's position.
visceralFunction.respiratoryLung: The lungs contain gas-exchange surfaces that allow oxygen to enter the blood and carbon dioxide to leave it; microscopic units are not shown separately.
visceralFunction.respiratoryUpper: Nasal structures help filter, warm, and humidify incoming air before it passes to the pharynx and lower airways.
visceralFunction.digestiveOral: The mouth and salivary structures receive, chew, and moisten food and begin digestion.
visceralFunction.digestiveOesophagus: The esophagus moves swallowed food to the stomach through coordinated muscular contractions.
visceralFunction.digestiveStomach: The stomach stores and mixes food with gastric secretions, beginning protein digestion before contents pass to the small intestine.
visceralFunction.digestiveIntestine: The intestines continue digestion and absorb nutrients and water; the detailed role varies by segment.
visceralFunction.digestiveLiver: The liver produces bile and performs many metabolic functions; the gallbladder stores and releases bile into the intestine.
visceralFunction.digestivePancreas: The pancreas releases digestive enzymes and bicarbonate into the small intestine; it also has endocrine roles not represented by this model.
visceralFunction.digestiveSupport: These structures help support, cover, or organize the abdominal organs.
visceralFunction.digestiveGeneral: Part of the digestive system; its general role is suggested by the anatomical name and position.

visceralRoute.respiratoryRoute: Nose or mouth → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi and bronchioles → lungs
visceralRoute.digestiveRoute: Mouth → pharynx → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine
visceralRoute.sharedRoute: Air passes from the pharynx toward the larynx, while food passes toward the esophagus; swallowing helps direct the two pathways.

circulationDisclaimer: 676 individually selectable structures. Lungs and capillary beds are not modeled; educational use only.
circulationDetailsOverview: This separately selectable mesh corresponds to “{{name}}” in the source anatomical atlas.
circulationDetailsLocation: The source identifies it as a {{side}} structure in the {{circuit}} circuit. Its exact position is shown by the selected 3D mesh.
circulationDetailsCaveat: This is an educational anatomical model, not a clinical reference. The source does not include lungs or individually modeled capillary beds.
circulationDetailsReference: Part names and geometry come from the credited Z-Anatomy / BodyParts3D model. Descriptions explain general circulation roles and do not replace clinical references.

circulationFunction.pulmonaryTrunk: Leaves the right ventricle and divides into the pulmonary arteries, carrying oxygen-poor blood toward the lungs.
circulationFunction.pulmonaryArtery: Carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs; pulmonary arteries are the exception to the usual oxygen-rich arterial flow.
circulationFunction.pulmonaryVein: Returns oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium; pulmonary veins are the exception to the usual oxygen-poor venous flow.
circulationFunction.aorta: The main systemic artery, carrying oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle into the body's arterial branches.
circulationFunction.venaCava: Returns systemic venous blood to the right atrium.
circulationFunction.atrium: An atrium receives blood returning to the heart and passes it to a ventricle.
circulationFunction.ventricle: A ventricle pumps blood out of the heart; the right ventricle serves the pulmonary circuit and the left the systemic circuit.
circulationFunction.valve: Heart valves help maintain one-way flow. The precise direction depends on the named valve and its position.
circulationFunction.arteryPulmonary: Carries oxygen-poor blood away from the right side of the heart toward the lungs.
circulationFunction.arterySystemic: Part of the systemic arterial tree. These vessels generally carry oxygen-rich blood from the aorta toward named organs and tissues.
circulationFunction.veinPulmonary: Returns oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
circulationFunction.veinSystemic: Returns blood from named organs and tissues toward the right side of the heart.
circulationFunction.coronaryArtery: Supplies oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle (myocardium). The named coronary artery indicates its branch; individual branching patterns vary.
circulationFunction.coronaryVein: Returns blood from the heart muscle through the coronary veins toward the right atrium, commonly via the coronary sinus.
circulationFunction.heart: Part of the heart's pumping or valve apparatus; the exact role depends on the named structure.
circulationFunction.other: The source classifies this as another cardiovascular structure. Its precise role depends on the anatomical name shown above.

selectCirculationPart: Select a heart or vessel structure on the model
pulmonaryFlow: Right ventricle → pulmonary trunk and arteries → lungs → pulmonary veins → left atrium
systemicFlow: Left ventricle → aorta and arteries → body tissues → veins and venae cavae → right atrium
completeFlow: Pulmonary: heart → lungs → heart. Systemic: heart → body → heart.

helpBody: Rotate with the left mouse button or one finger. Zoom with the wheel or pinch. Pan with the right mouse button or two fingers. Search in English or Arabic, or browse the regions. Selecting a structure focuses the camera and opens its details. Press Escape to close the panel, and use system filters and isolation controls to explore the models.
sourceGeometry: Original anatomical geometry. Teeth and cartilage are excluded; sternum parts are composed into one adult bone.
